actual_prerequisite_review.conclusion: Finite positive masses and positive fixed kernel width give a finite-dimensional autonomous vector field on the positive-density domain; supplied pressure is continuously differentiable and no continuum convergence is imported.

Compact convex K keeps each segment in the positive-density domain. Finite pressure derivative extrema and finite kernel gradient/Hessian bounds give the declared componentwise Lipschitz constants and finite block maximum. Euler independently assumes its chosen uniform B and a valid Lipschitz upper bound L; it does not infer B from the Lipschitz constant.

Continuity makes U open; a small compact convex box has positive density minima and local Lipschitz F. Picard–Lindelof on R times U supplies a local C1 trajectory. The Euler theorem separately assumes the exact trajectory exists on its whole positive horizon, so no unsupported global-existence conclusion is used.
The real inequality applies at nonnegative hL. It also gives exp(L(T-kh))>=1 for k<=n, so together with exponential addition the proof bounds exp(khL) by exp(LT) without a hidden extra theorem.
Repeated real addition gives exp(hL)^k=exp(khL) for the finite integer step count and factors the terminal comparison.

The autonomous field is continuous on the open R times U domain, state dimension is positive, and [0,T] has at least two points. On each used subinterval [kh,(k+1)h] the solution has the required componentwise continuous derivative and ordered integral identity.

Each position/velocity Euclidean block and real internal-energy block has triangle and homogeneity properties; the finite maximum over N positive blocks is a norm. No change of norm constant is inserted.

Only ordered time intervals of length h or s>=0 are used, avoiding the reversed-integral sign trap. Continuous block integrands have integrable Euclidean norm; taking a finite maximum gives max_i integral norm(g_i)<=integral max_i norm(g_i). The zero-length interval and zero block integrals require no division.

complete_current_proof_review.derivation: For t=kh with k<n, the full exact segment through t+h stays in K. Volterra and uniform B give norm(z(t+s)-z(t))<=Bs. Lipschitz L bounds the defect integrand by LBs, giving local defect LBh^2/2 after ordered integration. All integrands are continuous.

Assuming only the currently established Zk in K, triangle inequality and Lipschitz give one-step perturbation factor 1+hL; the exact-start defect adds LBh^2/2. Evaluating the next Euler state requires F only at Zk, so next-step membership is not assumed circularly.

Conditional iteration from e0=0 yields LBh^2/2 times the finite geometric sum. For L>0 its ratio denominator hL cancels to Bh/2((1+hL)^k-1). For L=0 the local defect is zero and error remains zero, avoiding division by L. Exponential addition and 1+x<=exp(x) give the stated uniform E_h for k<=n.

Positive distance from K-complement makes each exact state lie in K. Starting with exact initialization, conditional recurrence gives e(k+1)<=E_h<delta before next membership is concluded. A point outside K would have distance from the exact state at least delta, contradicting this strict error bound. Finite induction gives every claimed state and the error maximum.
